videos.title: The Green Hill by John Fletcher
videos.description: 4 Extra celebrates the 80th birthday of actress Diana Quick - born 23d November, 1946. In 1984, the perfectly preserved body of a man was found in a peat bog in Cheshire. He had received blows to the head, had been strangled and drowned. The press dubbed him Pete Marsh. Archaeologists now believe he lived at the time of the Roman invasion, that he was a druid, and was the willing victim of ritual sacrifice. This is his story. Written by John Fletcher. Lovernios .... Kim WallBoudica ....

videos.title: Desert Island Discs Revisited
videos.description: Actor Dame Joan Plowright is cast away by Sue Lawley. Joan has been at the forefront of her profession since she first appeared at the Royal Court Theatre in London half a century ago. In those days she was identified with the new wave, appearing in plays by writers such as Arnold Wesker and John Osborne. She went on to make her name in more established roles - winning Actress Of The Year for her performance as Shaw's 'St Joan'.

videos.title: David Attenborough's Life Stories
videos.description: The jungle canopy is one of the most inaccessible places to reach in the entire natural world. Sir David Attenborough was one of the first to film high in the treetops.

videos.title: Poetry Extra
videos.description: The poet Daljit Nagra revisits the BBC's poetry archive, choosing The Stately Pleasure Dome. And Daljit reads from his Poetry Extra Book of the Month, Crowd Voltage by John McCullough, choosing Popcorn. Poet Michael Symmons Roberts gets under the glowing domes of Manchester's Intu Trafford Centre, the largest shopping centre ever seen in the UK when it was built in 1998, to argue that it makes a unique poetic and architectural statement.

videos.title: How to Be Champion: Omnibus
videos.description: A twenty-something divorcee discovers her comedy talent. Sarah Millican reads from her frank and occasionally outrageous memoir, How to be Champion.

Ishmael, now in middle age, looks back on his younger self and remembers how this voyage of a lifetime began. Herman Melville's 1851 novel dramatised in two parts by Stef Penney. Ishmael..... Trevor White Young Ishmael..... PJ Brennan Captain Ahab..... Garrick Hagon Peter Coffin..... Howell Evans Queequeg..... Sani Muliaumaseali'i.
